newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile lower house approves Canada free trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile lower house approves Canada free trade deal.

text.p: Chile's lower house of Congress overwhelmingly approved a free trade agreement with Canada.

By a vote of 78 to 21, with 10 abstentions, the Chamber of Deputies approved the treaty that will phase out trade barriers between the two countries. President Eduardo Frei and Prime Minister Jean Chretien signed the agreement last year.
To become law, the treaty will now also have to be passed in the Senate, which is controlled by Frei's right-wing opponents and where the treaty is likely to face stronger opposition.
Objections to the treaty included its provisions on labor and the environment, which opponents said could impinge on Chile's local legislation in those areas.
Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat made a strong pitch for the agreement in recent days after news reports suggested opposition to it was growing.
